mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals a sharp demand contraction, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative following a double-digit decline in GDPC1 YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises by more than 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months indicates reduced household investment and consumption momentum, which depresses corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 4% for four consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which supports higher corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive quarters of GDPC1 > 4% annualized growth.
